title: Offline canary harness and telemetry contract for private deploy upgrades
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating fully isolated (zero-egress) Private/VPC clusters have limited ability to validate operator upgrades safely. Current upgrade acceptance relies on operator-level health checks and manual staging; teams report uncertainty about whether an upgrade will roll forward safely in low-bandwidth, split-DNS, or restrictive KMS environments.

Goal: Define a self-contained, reproducible 'offline canary harness' + telemetry contract that operators can run inside air-gapped Private deployments to validate upgrades before wide rollout. The harness must permit simulation of common failure modes (partial image corruption, KV cache warm-start failure, DNS partition) without requiring external network access, emit deterministic telemetry that Redwood control plane or on-prem observability can ingest, and specify human-in-loop thresholds for automatic rollback.

Non-goals: Designing the on-prem observability backend; changing existing customer KMS integrations (we will specify expectations but not re-implement KMS drivers). Not implementing an automated global orchestrator — this is a local validation harness and operator contract for Private clusters.
assumptions: 1) Customers will run harnesses on a staging subset of nodes with identical network policy to production. 2) Operator images and artifacts are provided via customer's mirror or offline media. 3) Minimal CLI tooling is acceptable; customers may wrap into their operator lifecycle tools. 4) We can require a lightweight telemetry emitter that writes to local files and, if configured, to the customer's telemetry aggregator (no outbound internet required).
requirements:
(R1) Offline Canary Harness: a packaged binary and k8s manifest that can run entirely offline (no egress) and exercise operator lifecycle: image pull from local registry, manifest apply, preflight health probes, staged component restart, and KV cache recovery test.
(R2) Failure Simulators: must include toggles for simulated image checksum mismatch, node-level disk pressure, controlled DNS split resolution, and simulated KMS rotation failure.
(R3) Deterministic Telemetry: harness produces a compact, schema-defined telemetry bundle (JSONL) summarizing test phases, latencies, error codes, and sampled traces. Schema must be stable across minor releases.
(R4) Human-in-loop thresholds: define numeric thresholds for abort/rollback (e.g., >10% pod crashloop within 10m, >500ms median RPC increase, failed KV warm-start in 3 attempts).
(R5) Artifact validation: manifest-level signature checks against customer-supplied public keys and an offline verification mode with SHA256 sums.
(R6) Runbook hooks: the harness emits runbook pointers and remediation suggestions inline in telemetry outputs.
(R7) Minimal resource footprint: harness should be runnable within 2 vCPU and 4GB RAM for a staging slice, with option to scale up.
(R8) No external dependencies: must work without outbound internet and without Redwood control plane connectivity (but allow optional telemetry export when configured).
constraints:
- Must not require changes to customer KMS beyond documented policy requirements.
- Must be compatible with split-horizon DNS setups and non-default MTU values.
- Must be packaged for Kubernetes operator lifecycle manager currently supported by Private (helm+operator-operator).
success_metrics:
- 90% of customers using the harness report increased confidence in upgrades (survey) within the first two weeks.
- Post-rollout incidents attributed to undetected offline upgrade regressions reduced by 60% for customers who adopt the harness.
- Harness run completes end-to-end within 20 minutes for standard staging slice (2vCPU/4GB).
- Telemetry bundles conform to schema v1.0 and pass validation for 100% of harness runs in CI.
acceptance_criteria:
AC-1: Deliver an OCI bundle (tarball) containing harness binary, k8s manifests, and example configs with offline verification mode documented.
AC-2: Provide a deterministic telemetry schema document and a local validator binary that checks a telemetry bundle and returns pass/fail with human-readable failures.
AC-3: Demonstrate simulation of at least three failure modes (checksum mismatch, DNS split, KV warm-start failure) in an air-gapped lab and capture telemetry for each.
AC-4: Define numeric human-in-loop thresholds and a sample runbook; engineering to implement automated abort/rollback hooks in operator upgraders when thresholds exceeded.
AC-5: Provide an ops playbook (markdown) for on-call with step-by-step rollback, artifact revalidation, and emergency-image reapply using offline media.
AC-6: Security review completed and signed off by Security + Compliance team; SCA and artifact signature verification requirements documented.
AC-7: CI smoke pipeline that runs harness in a minimal simulated airgap (within Redwood CI) and validates telemetry outputs on every private-operator release.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Spec & Prototype): 2 weeks — produce spec, telemetry schema, and a PoC harness that validates one simple operator upgrade offline.
Phase 1 (Internal Beta): 4 weeks — package harness, validator, and runbook; run with two internal Private customers in staged upgrades.
Phase 2 (Customer Beta): 6 weeks — onboard 3 customers with different networking profiles (split DNS, low MTU, custom KMS). Collect feedback and tune thresholds.
Phase 3 (GA): gated on meeting success metrics and Security sign-off; publish bundle, docs, and include harness in private-operator release notes.
Fallback: If customers cannot run harness as-is due to operator incompatibilities, provide a lightweight adapter pattern and documented steps to integrate their operator manifests into the harness.
telemetry_spec:
- Format: JSON Lines (newline-delimited JSON) compressed optional with gzip.
- Required fields: run_id, timestamp, phase (preflight|deploy|postflight), component, metric, value, sample_unit, trace_id (optional), error_code (if any), runbook_link.
- Size limit: per-run bundle <= 5MB compressed for standard slice.
- Local validation: validator exits non-zero if required fields missing or if error_code present in a fatal phase.
- Retention guidance: customers should retain telemetry bundles for 90 days for audit and regression analysis.
runbook_summary:
- Pre-upgrade: verify local registry accessibility, check manifest signatures, run 'harness preflight' and confirm pass.
- During upgrade: monitor harness telemetry; if abort threshold tripped, follow automated rollback or manual 'operator rollback' steps.
- Post-upgrade: run 'harness postflight' and export telemetry bundle to internal observability; collect logs and file a support bundle if anomalies remain.
- Emergency reapply: steps to re-stage previous images from offline media and re-run signature validation.
- Contact points: oncall-priv-deploy (Slack), SE-owner, and Security escalation list.
comments: 2025-02-14 Ayesha Patel: Initial draft PRD submitted. Requested decision on whether harness should include automated rollback vs emit-only telemetry. Action: schedule design sync with Eng and Security.

2025-02-16 Marcus Chen: Engineering concerns - automated rollback inside airgapped clusters requires formal operator hooks; propose we implement abort signals and leave rollback implementation to customer operator or ongoing 'operator-upgrade-manager' work. Recommended acceptance: abort signal + documented rollback steps.

2025-02-17 Lina Torres (Security): Security checklist updated: artifact signature verification is mandatory; offline public key provisioning must be in runbook. Recommend threat model review included in Phase 1.

2025-02-18 Marcus Chen: PoC started. Early results: checksum simulator worked; DNS split simulation requires injecting hosts file into test pods for now. Estimating two-week engineering spike to make simulators robust.
2025-02-20 Ayesha Patel: Updated spec to require telemetry schema validator in ACs. Confirmed Security review required. Next: schedule customer beta with 3 customers in March.
